promiseAndScope.role: Select, implement or review a reified invocation when identity, dispatch, lifetime, undo or transport earns its cost; preserve an adequate direct call/callback.
promiseAndScope.baseline: Java 17 records/sealed types; Java 21 for non-preview type-pattern switches. New binding example uses Java 17-compatible syntax.
successCriteria: Find the caller's target-selection, state, lifecycle and repeat contract.
Distinguish receiver identity from receiver state and data snapshots.
Preserve exact undo only inside its stated reversible boundary; keep compensation separate.
Preserve durable command identity and unknown-effect recovery constraints.

findingsCorrected.finding: The prior live-receiver sketch used an unqualified order name without distinguishing a captured local from a reassignable field read at invocation. The creation-time target and execution-time active target can be different objects.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A deferred action can operate on the wrong target, or an automatic lambda-to-method-reference rewrite can break a legitimate execution-time selection contract.
findingsCorrected.correction: Make the two bindings explicit, retain both as valid under different caller contracts, distinguish live receiver state from identity, and preserve null-failure timing.
findingsCorrected.evidence: JLS 17 §§15.13.3 and 15.27.4; 16 executed Java assertions plus the four-run two-contract fixture matrix.

findingsReviewedWithoutChange: History updates preserve state/stacks under documented immutable/confined operation failures; redo branch invalidation and inverse pre-state ordering are explicit.
Compound commands distinguish local candidate publication from externally visible effects.
Captured mutable components, consistent snapshot ownership and managed-session lifetime are already addressed.
Durable issuance retains identity/payload/timestamp; concurrent deduplication and provider unknown-outcome recovery are explicit prerequisites.
An adequate Runnable/method reference remains a valid Command implementation; no bus or class-per-method is imposed.
changeSummary: Three files changed, 16 insertions and 5 deletions. Descriptions, metadata referrals and worked history/durable-settlement examples are preserved.

preserved: Direct methods/callbacks as adequate alternatives to named command classes and buses.
Command/event semantic ownership and dispatcher validation.
Stable wire names, versioned intents, scoped retry identity and durable unknown-effect handling.
Snapshot depth, alias protection, synchronization/confinement and resource lifetime.
Exact inverse/memento versus compensation, stack order, compound failure boundary and redo invalidation.
Per-command outcome ownership, terminal failure routing and behavior-based checks.
replaced: Ambiguous single live-receiver lambda with explicit binding-time alternatives.

walkthroughs.kind: Structured reviewer reasoning; separate from runtime controls and not an actor evaluation.
walkthroughs.case01: A later active-field replacement redirects the existing lambda to B, contradicting creation-time target selection. Bind A while preserving A's live state.
walkthroughs.case02: Execution-time selection deliberately follows the field to B; retain the lambda. The same binding change valid in case 01 would be a regression here.

evaluationInstructions: Only target.selection differs between inputs; state.observed remains execution in both. Supply one input and the skill version to each actor, withholding criteria, reviewer report, technical probe and candidate fixture. Cases are known development examples, not unseen holdouts.

sources.supports: Lambda creation and body invocation are separate, supporting deferred field evaluation in the illustrated body.
sources.limit: The later field value is reliable in the example's confined execution; arbitrary unsynchronised mutation is outside that contract.
